item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded: My initial idea with this was a device that killed people because it doesn't work well, not because it's inherently malicious. Conceptually, the device would be used to remove traumatic memories in a therapeutic context and then, if they were important memories, they could be reimplanted in someone else or the original host for review. Unfortunately, I couldn't figure out how to come out and say 'the damn thing's busted, it's not supposed to cause the long-term damage it does', without some seriously odd writing implying omniscience on the part of the researchers. They don't know how the damn thing works, how can they know if it's working well?
